essayTitle: Report on the Class Clean-up Programme
source: SPM 2026 Trial · Terengganu (MPP3) · English Paper 2 · Part 3 Q5 · Report, 200–250 words
paragraphs: The clean-up programme took place on Saturday, 15 August 2026, from 8.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon. It was organised by Class 5 Cengal to promote a greener environment in our school area. A total of 35 students and two teachers took part. The main objective was to instil a sense of responsibility among students towards their surroundings.

First and foremost, we collected litter around the school compound and along the road outside the school gate. Armed with gloves and garbage bags, we gathered more than 20 bags of rubbish, mostly plastic bottles and food wrappers. Furthermore, we cleared the clogged drains and sorted the recyclable items. This helped prevent stagnant water, which can become a breeding ground for Aedes mosquitoes. Some students also planted flowering shrubs near the canteen to beautify the area.

Firstly, the school could hold a monthly "Green Saturday" so that cleaning up becomes a routine. Regular practice would help students cultivate the habit naturally. Secondly, a class cleanliness competition could be introduced. Attractive rewards would spur every class to keep its surroundings spotless.

In conclusion, the programme was a great success. Many participants said they would now think twice before littering. It is hoped that every student will play their part in keeping our school clean and green.
